# menu.List: focus neither opens a submenu nor closes the one it left

## Context

The operator's framing while scoping the menu stack, and the piece deliberately left out of #18759 and #18760 so each could be reviewed on its own:

> to SHOW sub-lists, focus and hover could be the better UX. also meaning: arrow up or down, when a child list is shown for the current item should hide it again.

Both halves are now measurable on `dev` (`17f5a83b95`, with #18761 / #18765 / #18766 merged). Two witness arms, run in the component harness against a three-item menu whose first item has children:

| witness | driven | result |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — a hovered submenu survives the focus moving away | hover `Share` → 2 menus → focus the first item → `ArrowDown` (focus on `Rename`) → wait out the 200 ms rest | **2 menus.** `Share`'s submenu is still showing under an item that no longer has focus |
| **B** — focus alone opens nothing | focus `Share`, wait out the rest delay | **1 menu.** A pointer rest shows the submenu; a keyboard rest on the same item does not |

Witness A is a defect: a submenu is a child of the item it belongs to, and the item lost focus. Witness B is the missing half of #18759 — the config is spelled `showSubMenuOnHover`, and the implementation took "hover" literally.

## The Problem

`showSubMenu()` has had a non-focusing preview mode since #18759 (`focus=false`), so the mechanism the keyboard needs already exists — what is missing is a caller and a symmetric hide.

- **Nothing binds focus to a rest.** `menu/List.mjs#onItemMouseEnter` is wired to `mouseenter` only (`construct`), and it is the only path into `onItemRest()`.
- **Nothing hides on the way out.** `selection/ListModel#onKeyDownUp` and `#onKeyDownDown` are empty placeholders (`src/selection/ListModel.mjs:40`, `:64`), and `selection/menu/ListModel` does not override them — arrow movement is the main thread's Navigator moving focus, which the App Worker never sees as a menu event. `hideSubMenu()` is called from a rest on a leaf, from `onSelect`, from `leaveSubMenu()` and from `afterSetMenuFocus`; nothing calls it when focus moves between siblings.

The trap this leaf has to get right: **`ArrowRight` moves focus INTO the submenu.** A naive "focus left the parent → hide" rule closes the submenu the same keystroke just opened. The hide must fire when focus lands on a *sibling* of the parent, not on a descendant of the submenu.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/menu/List.mjs#onItemRest(nodeId)` — the preview entry point, already liveness-guarded, already exclusive through `showSubMenu()`.
- `src/menu/List.mjs#showSubMenu(nodeId, record, focus=false)` — shows without selecting and without moving focus, via `component.Base#focusOnMount`.
- `src/menu/List.mjs#onFocusEnter` / `#onFocusLeave` — the menu already observes focus at the LIST level (`menuFocus`), including `isInteractionPath(data.oldPath)`, which is the discriminator the sibling-vs-descendant rule needs. The item-level focus signal is `component.Base`'s focus events with their `path`.
- `src/menu/List.mjs` configs `showSubMenuOnHover` and `subMenuHoverDelay`, read from `getRootMenu()`.

## The Fix

1. A focus landing on an interactive item is a rest, on the same `showSubMenuOnHover` / `subMenuHoverDelay` contract as a pointer rest, and takes the same non-focusing `showSubMenu(..., false)` path. The submenu appears; focus stays on the parent until the user presses `ArrowRight`.
2. A focus landing on an item whose sibling has a submenu showing hides that submenu — and a focus moving into the submenu does not.

**Naming fork, recommendation first.** `showSubMenuOnHover` ships on `dev` as of this morning and is unreleased.

| option | for | against |
|---|---|---|
| **keep the name** (recommended) | zero churn; the docblock can say the switch covers both rests | the word "hover" under-describes the keyboard half |
| rename to `showSubMenuOnRest`, no alias | the name matches the behaviour while the cost is at its lowest | a public config renamed inside a day, and the Contract Ledger carries both spellings |

Recommendation is the first row, decided here rather than escalated (reversible in one line). Reviewers who disagree can overturn it in a round.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — focus resting on a parent item shows its submenu without selecting it and without moving focus off the parent, gated by `showSubMenuOnHover` and delayed by `subMenuHoverDelay`.
- [ ] **AC-2** — focus moving to a sibling hides a submenu that was showing, whether a pointer rest or a focus rest opened it. Witness A above is the red-first state.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `ArrowRight` still opens and enters the submenu: focus moving into a descendant must not hide it. A CONTROL arm that would pass under a naive rule and fail under the correct one.
- [ ] **AC-4** — hover and focus do not fight: with the pointer resting on one parent and focus moved to another, exactly one submenu is showing, and the arms say which one wins rather than tolerating either.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the keyboard cascade and pointer rest arms from #18760 / #18759 stay green, and the new arms are red-first against `dev`.
- [ ] **AC-6** — `showSubMenuOnHover: false` suppresses the focus rest exactly as it suppresses the pointer rest.

## Out of Scope

- Selection on navigate. The focus model is the settled outcome of #18760: arrows move focus, Enter / Space / click activate.
- Any change to `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` / `Escape` semantics beyond AC-3's guard.
- The `showSubMenuOnHover` rename — the fork is recorded above; taking the second row is a one-line follow-up, not this leaf's job.
- `menu/List.spec.mjs`'s pointer-rest measurement flake — #18772.

## Avoided Traps

- **Hiding on any focus change.** `ArrowRight` moves focus into the submenu; a rule that does not distinguish descendant from sibling closes what it just opened. AC-3 exists to make that failure visible instead of plausible.
- **Re-deriving the rest through a second timer.** `onItemRest` and `cancelRest` already own the delay, its cancellation and the liveness check; a focus path with its own timer would be a second source of truth for the same UX.
- **Taking focus into the submenu on a focus rest.** That is the `focus=true` path and belongs to `ArrowRight`; a preview that steals focus makes `ArrowDown` unusable.
- **Asserting "a submenu is open" by counting levels.** #18759 measured that a close and a reopen inside one worker task are invisible to a level count; where a transition is the subject, count removals.

## Related

- #18758 / #18759 / #18760 — the three merged leaves this completes. #18765's `component.Base#focusOnMount` is the mechanism AC-1 reuses.
- #5123 — the Navigator change that moved menus to focus-driven keynav and left these two gaps.
- #2585 — the 2021 hover-expand request, stale-closed.

- 2026-09-16T11:58:13Z @tobiu referenced in commit `08f9d60` - "feat(menu): focus rests like a pointer rests (#18780) (#18783)

A pointer resting on a parent item previewed its submenu; the keyboard did neither half. Arrowing
onto a parent showed nothing, and arrowing OFF a parent left the submenu a hover had opened standing
under an item that no longer had focus.

Both come from one signal. `manager.Focus` fires `onFocusMove` on the closest component the old and
new focus paths share, which for an item-to-item move is the menu itself — so the menu now rests on
the item focus landed on, through the same timer, the same `showSubMenuOnHover` switch and the same
non-focusing `showSubMenu()` the pointer uses. One list resting on a new item drops what the previous
one showed, so the stale submenu closes without a rule of its own.

The case that needs no guard is the one a plausible implementation gets wrong: `ArrowRight` moving
focus INTO the submenu shares an ancestor of both menus, not this menu, so it never reaches
`onFocusMove` and the submenu it just opened stays open. A rule keyed on `onFocusLeave` would close
it — measured, and its CONTROL arm is the only one that reds under that mutation.

`Down onto a parent shows nothing` was asserted by a keyboard-cascade arm from #18760. That is the
behaviour this ticket reverses, so the arm now covers `Right on a leaf` and `Left in the root`, and
the focus-rest describe owns what Down does.

component.Base's onFocusMove docblock named `opts.newPath`; manager.Focus passes `path` and `oldPath`
plus the component. Corrected while relying on it — this is the hook's first implementer."
